open_points.text: `size` is the number of bytes that were read, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of
open_points.question: Is `size` the length of the logical byte sequence hashed into `source_id`, or the cumulative number of bytes read from the file, including repeated reads; and what corresponding rule applies when a rejected observation has no `source_id`?
options: The length of the single logical source-byte sequence hashed into `source_id`; for rejected files, the length of the logical source bytes successfully obtained before rejection.
The cumulative count returned by every file read, including repeated reads of the same bytes.
The source file's metadata size whenever no `source_id` is present.
open_points.default_guess: Use the length of the logical source-byte sequence hashed into `source_id`, and for a rejected file use the number of logical source bytes successfully obtained before rejection, falling back to metadata only when none were obtained.

witness.initial: A listed file has metadata size 100 bytes and stable 100-byte content.
events: The deliverer reads the 100 bytes once to inspect or decode them and again to compute `source_id`.
The calling flow reads the resulting SourcePhotoObservation.
outcomes: `size` is 100 because it is the length of the byte sequence hashed into `source_id`.
`size` is 200 because 200 bytes were cumulatively read from the file.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different `size` for the same file and `source_id`.
